title: POC gating playbook and acceptance matrix
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-04 15:00 UTC | Duration ~52m | Attendees: Jordan, Maya (Redwood); Carlos, Aisha, Tom (Beacon)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we've got about 50 minutes, so let's run through the acceptance gating playbook and the pass/fail matrix for the pilot.
[00:18] Carlos: Yep, thanks. We want to lock in the go/no-go criteria today — timeline's tight, fiscal sign-off by mid-December.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Quick note, I'll be the technical lead on this call for Redwood, so I'll cover benchmarks and how we'll run the tests.
[00:32] Aisha: Sounds good. We're mainly concerned about latency at peak, cost per 1k tokens, and a couple of quality measures — hallucination rate and F1 on our entity extraction set.
[00:44] Jordan: Perfect. I'll start with the high-level framing — acceptance will be gated on four primary SLOs: latency (p95), throughput (sustained QPS), cost/unit, and a quality/regression threshold. We'll also have secondary checks like SSO integration and audit log visibility.
[00:58] Tom: Procurement will also need a simple pass/fail statement we can attach to the contract — ideally a binary outcome with the metrics appended.
[01:05] Maya: Ok, diving in — baseline assumptions from Beacon: expected steady-state traffic 30k requests/day, typical payload average 400 tokens, peak bursts up to 180 QPS sustained for short windows, 99.9% availability target. Do I have that right?
[01:21] Carlos: That's right. Also 70% of requests are short context (<=256 tokens), 30% long (>=1k) for document summarization.
[01:31] Maya: Good. For the POC we'll scope three benchmark workloads: 1) Short-chat style 256 tokens, 2) long-doc summarization 1k-2k tokens, 3) mixed real traffic replay for throughput. Each workload will have three runs: cold start, warm cache, and sustained 30-minute run to capture queuing behavior.
[01:54] Aisha: How are you defining "warm cache"?
[01:58] Maya: Warm cache = KV cache primed with top 20% prefixes from your traffic replay; simulates typical production hit rate. We'll capture cache hit/miss, effective per-token latency. Note: earlier notes in our deck said "K-V cash" which is a transcribe typo — just to be clear.
[02:12] Jordan: On pass/fail thresholds — we're proposing the following: latency p95 <= 120ms on short requests; p95 <= 600ms on long summarization; throughput >= 150 QPS sustained for mixed replay; token cost delta <= +20% vs your internal target; quality: hallucination measured by false-entity rate <= 2% and NER F1 drop no more than 3% vs your baseline. If a single primary SLO misses by more than 10% we mark it as a fail unless compensating wins on others — we can define a weighted rubric.
[02:45] Carlos: That seems reasonable but we need to see the weightings — our product team cares about quality more than cost.
[02:52] Jordan: Understood. Proposed weighting: quality 40%, latency 25%, throughput 20%, cost 15%. If total weighted score >= 80% it's a go. If between 65%-80% leadership review, below 65% is no-go.
[03:07] Aisha: Is that score deterministic? Who runs the scoring?
[03:10] Maya: Redwood will run the benchmark harness, produce the raw metrics CSVs and a scoring spreadsheet. We'll also provide scripts so Beacon can re-run locally. The scoring spreadsheet is deterministic given the metric values; we'll repo both the raw logs and the interpreted slides.
[03:25] Tom: From procurement POV, we want the scoring and the test artifacts in a form we can attach. CSV + PDF summary is fine.
[03:31] Jordan: Noted. We'll deliver: raw per-request logs (anonymized), per-run CSV, scoring workbook, and a 1-page pass/fail certificate. Link to template: https://app.redwood.com/poc/templates/gating-playbook (note: placeholder).
[03:46] Carlos: How long will the benchmark window be?
[03:50] Maya: We usually propose a 5-day window — two days for setup and smoke, two days for the three benchmark runs, and one day for analysis & review. In compressed mode we can do it in three days but the risk of spurious variance goes up.
[04:03] Carlos: We need results in time for the budget meeting on Dec 16, so three-day compressed would be risky. Let's plan 5 days, starting Nov 24 earliest?
[04:12] Jordan: That's fine. That gives us time to get access keys and SSO details. Speaking of which — security checks: SSO/SAML test, SOC2 attestation review, KMS integration for private deployment if needed.
[04:26] Aisha: We will need audit logs to show data residency and request traces for compliance.
[04:30] Maya: We'll provide audit log exports and can run the POC inside your VPC via Redwood Private if you want to test KMS/HSM. That extends setup by 2-3 days for networking.
[04:42] Tom: That might be necessary for the procurement sign-off — can we mark it as optional on the acceptance matrix?
[04:47] Jordan: Yes, we'll put infra/security checks as secondary gates — must pass only if Beacon opts into Private mode. If you stay hosted we supply encrypted transit and at-rest encryption, plus SOC/ISO docs.
[04:59] Carlos: Back to metrics — a question on failure modes: if long summarization p95 spikes but throughput and short latency are fine, does that kill the POC?
[05:07] Maya: Not necessarily. That's where the weighted score helps. Also we'll look at model variants — Redwood can route to a quantized vs full-precision variant. If quality drops for long docs we can try a higher-capacity model for the long workload and test the failover.
[05:20] Aisha: Can you simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbors in Dedicated?
[05:24] Maya: For Dedicated pools we'll run contention tests by injecting background load and measuring tail latency. We'll include those as an optional extra.
[05:31] Jordan: Now reporting format — raw CSVs with columns: timestamp, request_id, input_length, output_length, latency_ms, model_variant, cache_hit, error_code, token_cost. Analysis slides will include the pass/fail matrix, weighted score breakdown, time-series p95 plots, and a short runbook for remediation steps.
[05:50] Carlos: Will you provide the scoring workbook ahead so we can sanity check weights?
[05:55] Maya: Yes — we'll push the scoring workbook to the shared drive by EOD tomorrow.
[05:59] Jordan: Okay let's capture explicit acceptance thresholds to sign today — I'll read them and ask for thumbs up. 1) Short p95 <= 120ms; 2) Long p95 <= 600ms; 3) Mixed throughput >= 150 QPS; 4) Hallucination false-entity rate <= 2%; 5) Token cost +/− <= 20% of your target. Weighted score >=80% equals pass.
[06:24] Carlos: Thumbs up from me for those thresholds, with the note that we expect Redwood to call out any test config deviations.
[06:31] Aisha: Agreed, but we want the ability to request reruns if we think the setup was off.
[06:36] Jordan: We'll allow one rerun per major deviation claim within the 5-day window.
[06:41] Tom: One practical ask — can you put the pass/fail certificate in a template that procurement can attach as an appendix?
[06:46] Jordan: Yes — we'll include a boilerplate certificate with metric snapshots and signature lines.
[06:50] Maya: Quick technical nit — for quality evals we'll run your entity extraction test set through the model outputs and compute F1; we need the labeled ground truth CSV by Nov 18.
[07:01] Carlos: We can share that by Nov 15.
[07:05] Jordan: Great. Any other outstanding blockers?
[07:08] Aisha: Need SAML test account and read-only access to your metrics S3 bucket if we run an in-VPC test.
[07:15] Maya: We'll send our mini-ops checklist with exact IAM roles and networking steps.
[07:20] Jordan: Cool — let's do a short recap.
[07:23] Jordan: Deliverables: 1) Scoring workbook and test plan (Redwood) by EOD Nov 5; 2) Beacon provides ground truth CSV and access by Nov 15; 3) POC window Nov 24-28 with runs and analysis; 4) Final results slide deck + pass/fail certificate by Dec 2.
[07:42] Carlos: That's aligned. Also add optional Dedicated contention test if we decide to evaluate that — decision by Nov 10.
[07:51] Tom: Procurement action — we need the template certificate and the CSV + PDF deliverables to be archived in the contract.
[07:58] Jordan: Will do.
[08:00] Maya: I'll follow up with the benchmark harness Git repo and the run scripts; link included in the follow-up. Apologies if some earlier deck slides referenced "Redwood Dedicate" — transcription/typo, our bad.
[08:12] Aisha: Haha, no worries.
[08:15] Jordan: Any final questions?
[08:18] Carlos: One last one — who owns the final sign-off?
[08:21] Aisha: Product leadership will own quality sign-off, procurement will own contractual acceptance, and engineering will own the infra checks. We'll coordinate.
[08:30] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks all, we'll send the scoring workbook tonight and the test plan tomorrow morning.
[08:36] Tom: Thanks everyone.

End transcript.
summary: Redwood and Beacon aligned on a 5-day POC window and a deterministic scoring rubric for go/no-go. Primary SLOs: short p95 latency, long p95 latency, mixed throughput, hallucination/NER quality, and token cost. Weighted scoring (quality 40%, latency 25%, throughput 20%, cost 15%) with >=80% pass. Deliverables and timeline agreed (scoring workbook by Nov 5, ground truth by Nov 15, run Nov 24-28, results by Dec 2). Security/integration checks and optional Dedicated contention tests noted.
next_steps: Redwood: send scoring workbook and test plan by 2025-11-05
Beacon: share labeled ground truth CSV by 2025-11-15
Decision on Dedicated contention test by 2025-11-10

Maya Chen: share benchmark harness repo and run scripts; due 2025-11-05
Carlos Ruiz: provide labeled entity ground truth CSV; due 2025-11-15
